title: Uncovering Separable and Composable Skill Mechanisms in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.30290v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent work has sought to localize the internal mechanisms underlying visual reasoning skills in vision-language models. These methods largely overlook separability and composability in both mechanism identification and evaluation. We propose separability and composability as two important desiderata for skill localization. Separability requires identified mechanisms to contribute primarily to their target skills while having limited effects on other skills, enabling precise diagnosis and targeted intervention. Composability requires skill mechanisms to be combinable to support complex tasks, allowing a small set of mechanisms to account for broader capabilities. In this work, we propose a multi-skill interpretability framework DISCO, built around these two properties. translated_title: 揭示视觉-语言模型中可分离与可组合的技能机制
translated_abstract: 近期的研究试图定位视觉-语言模型中视觉推理技能背后的内部机制。这些方法在机制识别和评估中都很大程度上忽视了可分离性和可组合性。我们提出将可分离性和可组合性作为技能定位的两个重要标准。可分离性要求所识别的机制主要对其目标技能做出贡献，同时对其他技能的影响有限，从而实现精确诊断和有针对性的干预。可组合性要求技能机制能够组合以支持复杂任务，使一小组机制能够解释更广泛的能力。在这项工作中，我们提出了一个围绕这两个特性构建的多技能可解释性框架DISCO。在机制识别方面，我们提出了可分离头选择方法，基于注意力头在各技能上的贡献来筛选特定技能的注意力头。在评估方面，我们……
tldr: 提出以可分离性和可组合性为两大核心标准的多技能可解释性框架DISCO，通过可分离头选择方法识别视觉-语言模型中特定技能的注意力头，实现对技能机制的精确诊断与可组合扩展。
en_tdlr: Proposes DISCO, a multi-skill interpretability framework that localizes skill mechanisms in vision-language models based on two desiderata—separability and composability—and identifies skill-specific attention heads via Separable Head Selection.
